<!-- screenshot: builder-new-domain-dialog -->
A domain is one business area with its own doctypes and its own data. You
build it in a **draft**: a private work area whose name starts with `_`.
When the model is ready, you publish it under its real name, and Facet
creates the live domain.

## When to use this

Open a draft when you design a new domain, or when you change a live domain
and want to test first. Co-editors work with you in the same draft, and
everyone who edits the draft keeps the right to edit the published domain.

:::note
A draft holds no production data. Documents you create while you test are
scratch. Publish copies the structure only — the [full
picture](/build/model/in-app/how-drafts-work/) has the one exception.
:::

## Before you start

- **The editor role.** Any account with the [`editor` role](/admin/people/roles-and-permissions/) can open a draft;
  you become its first editor.
- **Your name on the domain's Editors tab** to fork a live domain with
  **Edit existing**. A live domain lists no editors at first — not even the
  administrator. Open **Configure → Domains**, open the domain, open
  **Editors**, and add your account.
- **An administrator for co-editors.** Only an administrator can change the
  editor list of a domain.

## Steps

### 1. Open a draft

In the **Builder**, use **New domain** to start from nothing, or **Edit
existing** to fork a live domain. The dialog has two name fields:

| Field | Rule | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Label | Free text, up to 64 characters. | The name people see in the interface. |
| Domain id | Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; starts with a letter. | The name of the live domain you plan to publish. The draft itself keeps a temporary, autogenerated `_`-id. |

:::tip
Set the **Domain id** early. Facet checks the format when you save the
draft, so a typo fails at once and not at publish time.
:::

### 2. Add and change doctypes

Create the doctypes of your model (see [Design a
doctype](/build/model/data/design-doctypes/)). Inside a draft, Facet relaxes
the version rules: you can remove a field, change a type, or skip a version.
All other schema checks still run, and every script must compile.

The definition cache updates a second or two after you save. Re-test a
change after a short wait before you judge it.

### 3. Add co-editors

An administrator opens the domain's **Editors** tab and lists the accounts
that edit the draft with you. An editor cannot change this list — the rule
keeps the grant chain with the administrators. Co-editors of the draft keep
their rights on the published domain.

<!-- screenshot: editors-tab -->

### 4. Test in preview

Open the **Preview** tab. Facet then shows the draft in the live
application: you open pages, run actions, and create documents, all inside
the draft. Cross-domain references into live domains show no data during
preview, and schema edits send you back to the Builder.

<!-- screenshot: builder-preview -->

### 5. Run the checks

Open the **Check** tab. Facet lists the issues and notices for every doctype
in the draft. An empty draft reports that there is nothing to publish. Fix
the issues before you publish — see [Check before you
publish](/build/model/in-app/check-before-publish/).

### 6. Publish

Select **Publish**. In the dialog you choose the target name and the mode:

<!-- screenshot: publish-dialog -->

- **Fresh publish** — the target name must be free. Facet creates the domain
  and copies your doctypes.
- **Overwrite publish** — the target domain exists. Facet asks for a
  confirmation (**Publish over {name}**), and every doctype you changed must
  bump its schema version by exactly one, with a migration for the step (see
  [Change a live domain safely](/build/model/change-a-live-domain/)).

The dialog also offers **Import existing documents** — carry chosen scratch
doctypes' documents into the published domain. Leave it off unless you know
you want the test data.

Facet copies the co-editors to the published domain, files any cross-domain
grant tickets, and drops the draft. The report names each ticket and whether
data can flow yet.

## Example

The call below publishes a draft to a fresh domain named `orders`. Read the
API key from the `FACET_API_KEY` environment variable.

```sh
curl -k -X POST "https://facet.localhost:3443/Api/core/Domain/_3fjqk2m8p1xz/publish" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FACET_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"target_name": "orders", "overwrite": false}'
```

The response names the published domain and reports any grant tickets and
warnings. `-k` skips the certificate check of the local development address.

## Troubleshooting

### Publish refuses the target name

The name must be lowercase letters, digits, and dashes, and it must start
with a letter. A name that starts with `_` is a draft name. Fix the **Domain
id** field or the target name and publish again.

### Overwrite publish refuses a doctype

The live version and your draft version differ by more than one, or a
migration entry is missing. Raise the version one step at a time, or publish
to a fresh domain instead.

### I cannot fork a live domain

A domain with an open draft forks no second draft — Facet answers `409`.
Discard or publish the first draft, then fork again.

If Facet answers `403` with *"You must be an editor of domain …"*, the
domain's Editors list does not name you. Facet forks a live domain only
for an account the domain lists as an editor, and the Administrator is no
exception — a seeded domain starts with an empty list. Open
**Configure → Domains**, open the domain's **Editors** tab, add your
account, and fork again.

### My change did not appear at once

The definition cache updates a second or two after a save. Wait briefly and
test again.

### I cannot delete the live domain

Deleting a domain is an administrator action, and Facet refuses while one of
its drafts is open. Discard the draft first.
